### 2026-10-19 – # Start

**3h**

# Start
I did some quick research and looked around for parts I could use. I just wanted to start to be fair, I was a bit lazy. I opted for some Mx switches, potentiometers/ rotary encoders, some LEDs and resistors and an Xiao esp32C6. I also looked at a few other macro pads which include similar components.

![1000008564](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/916c6690846cbef67b2c39fef90d28e69001d1430c84b73973a887c678ebf61e.jpg)

## PCB schematic
 I designed the PCB schematic with net ports so all the components are neatly arranged. As you can see,  I the found parts/models for each component's circuit diagram and wired them together. Each switch to its own GPIO pin and the same with the other components.

![1000008565](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/7461a5e8634eb9efcc9fa7014eeb3420577c9d5b7acee35614c7684fa72fdcc9.png)

I used an esp32 C6, 9 Mx switches, 2 pec11r rotary encoders, and 3 Leds. I think this will give me lots of creative freedom do program it accordingly.

### 2026-10-19 – # The Cost of Laziness

**2.5h**

# The Cost of Laziness
This morning, as I mentioned in the journal, I just wanted to start, didn't really get a concrete plan fleshed out. Now today, I am changing the parts... (Ooops)

## Microcontroller
I found out that the Xiao esp32C6 usb c port doesn't do OTG (on the go) easily and I would have to relay data from the synth macro pad to my computer over WiFi, which would cause latency. For this reason, I decided to swap the microcontroller to a RP2040 zero, which has quite a lot of pins and can output data through the usb, but doesn't have WiFi or Bluetooth which I don't need. Thankfully I used net ports so it was easy enough to switch the boards around in the schematic.

![1000008566](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/ee444ea4275a845d711f8dc2ffb48b8dd355e50fe93baea4c1cca9d1d8fe8a43.jpg)
*Seeed Xiao esp32C6

![1000008567](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/684d2fe87ceaf10c4b64d401e5c2dc94f3b8276f4aeb8a5dbc6fcf344da2fc32.jpg)
*RP2040 zero

## Rotary encoders
When I was looking at rotary encoders to use I found 2, the PEC11R and the EC11. I look at the PEC11R and went for it because it was more 'premium'. However, when I was just looking for it online it was quite expensive and not commonly available. So, I found an EC11 circuit diagram and swapped the encoders around. I mean, they basically look the same and it is just the pinout which is slightly different.

![1000008569](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/7826d269b4efcce10fbc583959f54b47cf4975a83af96643ce9069d24e216f73.jpg)
*PEC11R

Once I realised that the microcontroller and rotary encoders were wrong/bad. I went over every other of the components I needed to make sure they were compatible.
